title: Sound
standard_text: Describe how sound is made by vibrations and travels through solids, liquids and gases; describe pitch and loudness; assess the effects of noise and technologies that protect or improve hearing. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Light and Sound)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on vibrations, how sound travels, pitch, loudness, echoes and noise pollution. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Fast vibrations give a high pitch; big vibrations give a loud sound.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every sound comes from something vibrating (moving back and forth quickly).

  • Sound travels through solids, liquids and gases, but not through empty space.
  • Pitch is how high or low a sound is. Faster vibrations make a higher pitch.
  • Loudness depends on the size of the vibrations. Very loud sounds can damage hearing.
  • An echo is sound reflected off a surface. Soft materials absorb sound.
Example

A ruler is twanged on a desk. It is made shorter. What happens to the pitch?

shorter part vibrates faster

Answer: higher pitch

Example

Can sound travel in space?

sound needs particles to vibrate

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up pitch and loudness.
  • Thinking sound travels best through air (it travels faster in solids).
  • Thinking sound can travel through empty space.

faq.q: What is the difference between pitch and loudness?
faq.a: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. Loudness is how strong or quiet it is.

faq.q: Why does sound travel faster in water than in air?
faq.a: The particles in liquids are closer together, so vibrations pass along more quickly.

faq.q: How can we reduce noise pollution?
faq.a: With noise barriers, soft materials that absorb sound, quieter machines and ear protection.
